title: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation

concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify the Early, Mature and Late Harappan phases and their approximate dates.
Students will explain how archaeologists reconstruct Harappan diet from plant and animal remains.
Students will interpret the evidence for ploughing, cropping and irrigation in Harappan agriculture.
Students will describe the Citadel, the Lower Town and the standardised bricks as signs of planning.
Students will explain how the drainage system reflects town planning.
Students will describe domestic architecture and the structures on the Citadel, including the Great Bath.
Students will evaluate what Harappan burials reveal, and do not reveal, about social differences.
Students will distinguish utilitarian objects from luxuries and interpret their distribution.
Students will describe the materials and techniques used to make Harappan beads.
Students will identify the evidence archaeologists use to locate centres of craft production.
Students will explain how the Harappans obtained raw materials from within the subcontinent.
Students will analyse the evidence for Harappan contact with Oman, Dilmun and Mesopotamia.
Students will explain how seals and sealings were used in long-distance communication.
Students will state the known features of the undeciphered Harappan script.
Students will apply the binary and decimal pattern of Harappan weights.

topics.title: Ancient authority and the end of the civilisation

concepts.learning_objective: Students will analyse the evidence for authority and the debate on rulers in Harappan society.
Students will explain the changes after c. 1900 BCE and the explanations offered for the decline.
Students will evaluate how re-examination of evidence changed the interpretation of an 'invasion'.

topics.title: Discovering the civilisation and problems of interpretation

concepts.learning_objective: Students will trace the roles of Cunningham, Sahni, Banerji and Marshall in discovering the civilisation.
Students will explain stratigraphy and how excavation methods affect the recovery of context.
Students will evaluate the difficulties of reconstructing Harappan religious practices.
